title: ReadFormatter: automatic elision for every AI read path
desc: One output-boundary formatter shared by skill read, file read, a11y read, find and skill search. Elides automatically when output would exceed the byte budget so it never spills to a file, keeps every unit recognisable, and lets --keep steer what survives and --budget lower the ceiling. Carries the measured marker arithmetic and the 30000-is-a-retreat-not-a-limit rule.
steps: WHAT IT IS: ONE output-boundary formatter for EVERY read path -- skill read, file read, a11y read, find, and skill search -- named by the owner 2026-09-04 as a service for AI readers. WHEN: you are adding or changing any command that prints a variable amount of text to an AI. HOW: hand it the ARRAY OF PARAGRAPHS plus the keep terms, the byte budget, the measured reserved bytes, and YOUR OWN retrieval command string for the footer; read wkappbot skill read wksplit-cs-utility-howto before touching a host file, because the hosts are past the 400-line cap and must REPLACE lines rather than add them. WHY: measured 2026-09-03 -- a study lock demanded three skills totalling 424KB, the transport spilled each to a file and returned a 2KB preview, and ZERO steps reached the reader. The lock was satisfied and nothing was learned. //why:dispatching smoke-fix sector needs score above 60-sonnet

A SPILL IS TOTAL LOSS THAT LOOKS LIKE CONTENT, which is why it goes unnoticed. WHEN: a result line says the output was too large and was saved to a file. HOW: treat the knowledge as NOT RECEIVED -- do not reason from the banner, and read wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the habit of proving receipt instead of assuming it. WHY: the preview is the command banner plus the header, which look exactly like a successful read; a session took THREE consecutive 424KB reads before noticing no step body had arrived, and skill search spilled identically at 69.9KB while merely looking for a place to file this skill. Filtering is not an escape either -- a knowledge-op carrying a pipe or redirect is refused by the harness, so the reader cannot grep its way out.

ELISION IS AUTOMATIC AND --keep ONLY STEERS. WHEN: wiring the formatter into any command. HOW: fire whenever the assembled output would exceed the budget, with or without --keep, and when it fires with no --keep print a usage hint showing THREE accepted forms, each with its own crisp example: (1) COMMA-LIST, no spaces, one flag, splits into several keywords -- --keep kw1,kw2,kw3 ; (2) QUOTED PHRASE, kept whole including any commas/spaces it contains -- --keep 'one exact phrase' ; (3) REPEATABLE FLAGS, one term or phrase per occurrence, for mixing keywords with a phrase -- --keep kw1 --keep kw2 --keep 'a phrase'. A quoted value containing a space is ALWAYS kept as one literal phrase, never split on its commas, so cramming multiple terms plus a phrase into ONE quoted value (e.g. --keep 'kw1,kw2,a phrase') silently searches for text that matches nothing -- use form (3) instead; follow wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring-howto for the proto-then-promote sequence. WHY: the first wiring gated everything behind a keep-terms count, so a plain read of a large skill still spilled -- the entire failure left intact by the change meant to remove it. Under the budget the output must remain BYTE-IDENTICAL to before, so a small read is never disturbed.

THE PER-UNIT MARKER IS UNAFFORDABLE AT SCALE BY CONSTRUCTION, so hoist the retrieval sentence into ONE SHARED FOOTER. WHEN: designing any truncation marker. HOW: leave a single ellipsis per elided unit, name the retrieval command once at the end, and verify by measuring marker bytes against content bytes as in wkappbot skill read proof-techniques-that-caught-real-defects. WHY: measured at 200 steps, per-unit markers cost 13892 bytes against 10037 of content -- 58 percent of the budget spent explaining what it hid. The shared footer took markers to 702 bytes, 6.5 percent. A per-unit cost multiplies by unit count while the budget stays fixed; a footer costs the same at 20 units as at 200.

THE BUDGET IS 30000 BYTES AND THAT IS THE RETREAT FROM THE LIMIT, NOT THE LIMIT. WHEN: setting, overriding, or raising any read budget, including a --budget flag. HOW: clamp --budget to the MINIMUM against the default so it can only LOWER and never raise, and never anchor the number to an unrelated buffer; run wkappbot skill read wkappbot-build-verify-workflow before shipping a change to a shared output path. WHY: the observed spill threshold is 32768, and the 2.7K gap is deliberate headroom for the banner, footer and hint that wrap the content -- a successor who reads 30000 as the hard limit sees slack, raises it, and removes the margin. The threshold is OBSERVED, not queried: it lives in the calling tool and this process cannot read it. EyeCmdPipeClient._charBuf is a 32768-CHAR internal conversion buffer whose equal magnitude is a COINCIDENCE and must never be used as its source, or the budget silently follows an unrelated change.

MEASURE DELIVERY ON REALISTIC PROSE, or the number is wrong in the flattering direction as easily as the harsh one. WHEN: reporting how much content survives elision. HOW: build the fixture from real step text or ordinary words of 4 to 12 characters, never synthetic filler, and report delivered bytes per unit alongside the marker total; the discipline is in wkappbot skill read proof-techniques-that-caught-real-defects. WHY: a synthetic fixture whose words were 400 characters long reported 24.2 Korean characters per step because word-boundary truncation dominated; the same code on realistic prose delivered 16442 content bytes and 34.7 characters per step at 200 steps -- ten to twelve Korean words, which was the acceptance question. The synthetic figure understated the feature by 64 percent. A test whose input cannot occur in production measures the test.
A11y read wiring: constant A11yReadComprehensionBudgetBytes (4000 bytes), apply formatter before A11yReadNodeList print loop (line 435-437)

RESULT: a11y read carries a COMPREHENSION budget of 4000 bytes while skill read and file read carry the TRANSPORT ceiling, and the two guard different failures. WHEN: wiring the shared formatter into a new caller and choosing which budget it passes -- measured 2026-09-04 on the session's own console, a11y read --content returned 224.2KB and the transport handed back a 2KB preview, while --tail 40 delivered ~1700 bytes whole. HOW: run wkappbot skill read a11y-command-cheatsheet for the read surface, then pass the caller's own named constant -- A11yReadComprehensionBudgetBytes for a11y read, the transport ceiling for skill and file read -- and never a literal, since a proto that invented 32000 was rejected for exactly that. WHY: the transport failure is a SPILL where output cannot survive the pipe, but a11y read fails by VOLUME -- a reader wanders a UI tree and tokens blow up with no spill at all -- so the same engine must be handed a smaller number rather than a second implementation; 4000 is the owner's stated budget and is NOT a measured figure, which matters because a number labelled measured gets built upon.

DECISION: a --keep check must compare the SAME read with and without the term, never assert that one NAMED unit survives. WHEN: writing a regression test or smoke check for keep-steering. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then run the read twice at the same budget, count the matched word in each output with grep -ci, and assert the count is HIGHER with --keep; the smoke gate does exactly this and reports 3x with it vs 0x without. WHY: measured 2026-09-04 -- keep matches CASE-INSENSITIVELY, so a term like FLOOR also matches every lowercase floor, several units qualify, and which of them survives is a BUDGET RACE decided by water-filling, not a contract. The first version of this check asserted one specific step would appear verbatim and FAILED on a fully working build, which is worse than no check: it accuses a correct binary. The contract keep actually offers is only that more of the matched content survives than without it. //why:exact-phrase-first pass uses same paragraphs list as fallback keyword pass

HOWTO: wire a NEW caller in four steps -- the engine is caller-agnostic, so extending it is a call site, never a copy. WHEN: adding elision to file read, a11y read, find, skill search, or any future read path. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision-ref for the traps, then (1) find the loop that PRINTS the units and collect them into a List<string> instead; (2) parse at the boundary with ReadFormatter.ParseKeepArgument(args) and ParseBudgetArgument(args), never inside the engine; (3) call ReadFormatter.FormatOutput(units, keepTerms, budget, ReadFormatter.CalculateReservedBytes(<every line your command prints AROUND the units>), <the exact command a reader runs to get the rest>) and print what it returns; (4) verify by running the STAGING binary directly, bin/wktest-core-manual-v<ver>.exe, never the canonical wrapper. WHY: measured 2026-09-04 on skill read -- 265500 bytes became 29391 under a 30000 ceiling with 22 units marked. Three rules the callers differ on: the UNIT is whatever your command repeats (a step, a line, an element, a result row), the BUDGET comes from your own named constant (a11y read passes a ~4000 comprehension budget where skill read passes the transport ceiling), and a RANKED list drops whole rows from the bottom rather than truncating within a row, because a half-printed result is useless while a shorter ranked list is still correct.

DECISION: mark a DROPPED unit in its own place with a leading ellipsis and a shortest-unique quote, never as a count in the footer -- owner design 2026-09-04. WHEN: implementing or reviewing what the reader sees when a whole unit is withheld rather than truncated. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision-ref for the marker arithmetic, then at the drop site leave a line carrying NO number that begins with the ellipsis and ends with a quoted fragment of the dropped unit -- three dots space quote -- so position alone distinguishes the two states: an ellipsis at the RIGHT END means that unit was cut short, an ellipsis at the LINE START means the whole unit at that position is gone. Pick the fragment as the SHORTEST UNIQUE PHRASE: try one word, and while it matches more than one unit widen by one word on each side until it is unique. WHY: a footer that says only 1 dropped gives the reader no way back except re-reading everything, which is the spill this feature exists to prevent; a quote left AT THE DROP SITE keeps the position and the surrounding context, and --keep already accepts a whole quoted phrase so the retrieval interface needs no new flag. Do NOT use step NUMBERS as the handle -- a number becomes a lie the moment steps are edited or reordered, while a phrase is attached to the content; numbers are the last resort when no unique phrase exists. And do not add a bracketed label such as dropped, because reusing the ellipsis costs nothing and this feature already measured markers at 58 percent of the budget before they were hoisted into one footer.

DECISION: wire BOTH layers and know what each buys -- a per-module call formats WELL, the TeeTextWriter first-flush hook merely formats. WHEN: deciding whether a new caller needs its own wiring once the output-boundary hook exists. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision-ref for the promotion traps, then wire the module when the output has UNITS worth respecting -- it knows its own boundaries, its slot priority, its budget and its retrieval command, so it drops WHY before HOW and every surviving unit stays recognisable -- and let the boundary hook cover everything else, where it can only cut by line because it does not know what the command was. WHY: the two are LAYERS, not alternatives. Module wiring is aim; the boundary hook is the net -- nothing escapes the ceiling even from a command nobody wired, including commands that do not exist yet. They do not fight either: a module that already fits its budget leaves the first flush with nothing to cut. Owner framing 2026-09-04: formatting in each module comes out prettier, while firing at the TeeTextWriter first flush just mechanically shortens.

DECISION: reserve the HEAD and the MANDATORY FOOTER before the allocator spends anything, because a budget that covers only the units is not a budget. WHEN: wiring this engine into any caller, or explaining why an elided read still spilled. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then measure EVERY line your command prints around the units -- the banner, the id/app/desc/audience/tags head, the trailing hints, AND the launcher frame that wraps your process -- as UTF-8 bytes rather than characters, and reserve the FULL closing block (not the floor) so the usage hint is paid for up front. Prove it by the BYTE COUNT OF THE WHOLE RESULT, never by the steps section. WHY: measured 2026-09-04 -- skill read reserved only the TAIL, so a 30000-byte ceiling delivered 30618 bytes and the transport spilled it, i.e. elision SUCCEEDED and the feature still failed at the exact case it exists for. Desc and Tags are unbounded and grow with the skill, so no fixed headroom constant can absorb them; the overflow scales with the content, not with the format. Two more defects of the same family sat beside it: reservedBytes was subtracted TWICE (once into contentCeiling, once again inside the allocator), and the mandatory hint was reserved only AFTER allocation so it silently disappeared on the two largest skills -- an element declared mandatory but funded last is not mandatory.

DECISION: a RANKED list gets its own allocator and loses whole rows from the BOTTOM, never a share of every row. WHEN: wiring this engine into any caller whose output order carries meaning -- skill search, skill list, find, any scored or sorted result set. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision for the budget contract, then pass rankedWholeUnits true so FormatOutput routes to ElideRankedWholeUnits, which fills from the top and STOPS at the first row that does not fit; never skip ahead to a later shorter row that would fit, because the order IS the ranking and a list that silently omits rank 8 while showing rank 9 is lying about the ranking. WHY: the general allocator water-fills and truncates whatever overflows a fair share, which is right for independent paragraphs where half a step still teaches something, and wrong for a result row you cannot act on -- you cannot run skill read on an id that was cut in half, while a SHORTER ranked list is still a completely correct answer to the query. The arithmetic decides it: fair-share breaks every row at exactly the moment the list is long enough to need shortening, since 500 rows against a 30000 budget is 60 bytes each and a row is about 120. Measured live 2026-09-04 on skill search harness -- 628 hits, 406 dropped whole, 0 truncated, footer carrying the real query rather than a placeholder.

RESULT: the final clamp used to drop keep-MATCHED units, defeating --keep whenever the match sat LAST -- fixed and live-verified 2026-09-04. WHEN: reasoning about what survives elision, or touching the clamp loop in ReadFormatter.Elision.cs. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then know that the clamp now tracks each survivor's ORIGINAL index and removes the last NON-matched unit first, falling back to a matched one only when no unmatched unit remains; order is preserved because RemoveAt shifts, never reorders. WHY: the allocator gave keep-matching units their share first and the clamp immediately threw them away, because it removed from the end knowing nothing about keepMatching. Reading opus-self-reflection-ref with a phrase unique to step 27 of 31 returned 0 truncated, 1 dropped, of 31 with that step ABSENT and no no-match line -- the term matched and was discarded. A mid-list match survived, isolating the cause to POSITION. This mattered more than it looks: --budget only lowers, so --keep is the ONLY retrieval interface, and new units are appended LAST, so it failed precisely on what a reader is most likely to hunt. The same command now returns 29 truncated, 1 dropped, of 31 with step 27 present in full -- an inversion control on a real read, not a fixture. AND THE OTHER HALF OF THAT SAME no-match LINE WAS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, found and fixed 2026-09-07: FormatOutput returns the paragraphs UNCHANGED without ever consulting keepTerms whenever the content already fits under the ceiling, so ElideByKeepTerms and its closing block are never reached and a term matching nothing produced NO notice at all. The guarantee lives in BuildClosingBlockMinimal, whose own comment says unmatched terms are MANDATORY because a reader who asked for something and got silence must know -- but the floor tier is built only on the path that elides, which is the one place a non-eliding read cannot go. MEASURED BOTH WAYS on staging v7.9.219 BEFORE the fix: a nonsense keep term against a SMALL skill printed nothing, while the same term against a LARGE skill printed the notice, so the behaviour depended on the SIZE of the skill rather than on whether the term matched. The repair adds one call before that early return, into ReadFormatter.UnmatchedNotice.cs, and the matching MUST stay identical to the elision path, a case-insensitive Contains on the lowercased paragraph, or the two halves of one feature will disagree about what counts as a match. VERIFY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON A REAL RUN: a nonsense term against a SMALL skill must print the notice, and a term that genuinely appears must still print nothing -- a version that always appends passes the first test alone. AND A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FAMILY, FIXED 2026-09-07: TruncateWithMatchWindow RETURNED AN EMPTY STRING for its three degenerate inputs -- empty text, empty match term, or a budget at or below zero. That does not decline to build a window, IT DELETES THE UNIT, and a caller could not tell the result from a unit whose content was genuinely empty. It now returns the input unchanged, which is the honest degenerate answer since the caller still owns the budget and the outer truncation path cuts it if it must. The empty-term case was the sharpest: an empty needle matches at index zero, so without the guard it degrades to a silent HEAD TRUNCATION wearing the appearance of successful steering. AND THE SIBLING FILE WAS AUDITED AND FOUND CORRECT, which closes its letter entry by measurement rather than by a change: CreateDropMarker already returns a bare ellipsis with NO empty quote pair on every degenerate path -- null or whitespace, a zero-word split, and the all-markdown-noise case where the content index runs past the end. An empty quote would be the real defect there, because the quote is the RETRIEVAL HANDLE a reader pastes back into keep, and an empty one is a path that leads nowhere. A comment now records the audit in the file so nobody re-opens it, and records that IsMarkdownNoise is NOT dead -- it is called from CreateDropMarker, and the earlier zero-call-site reading came from a grep that excluded the whole defining file and so hid the intra-file call. AND THIS CLOSES AN INHERITED ITEM: three descent letters carried an unfinished wish called the keep colon parser, a sector reproduced nothing because colons and commas both match correctly, and the real defect was this silence, which a reader would naturally describe as keep not working.

RESULT: the dropped-unit position marker is LIVE -- a whole unit that goes now leaves a line beginning with the ellipsis and carrying a shortest-unique quote, exactly as owner step 16 specifies. WHEN: reading elided output, or touching the FINAL CLAMP in ReadFormatter.Elision.cs. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then read any large skill and look for a line starting with the ellipsis -- measured 2026-09-04 on the staging binary, skill read opus-self-reflection returns a marker reading ellipsis then quote your own tool, alongside the footer count. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT TERMINATE, because the obvious implementation does not: the marker REPLACES the unit in place and STAYS, so the byte total falls from roughly a thousand to about thirty per drop; the loop tracks marked POSITIONS and skips them when choosing the next victim, or it re-picks the same slot forever; and only when every non-matched slot is already a marker does it begin removing markers from the end, re-indexing the marked set as it goes since removal shifts every later position. WHY THIS IS WORTH WRITING DOWN: the first two delegated attempts BOTH wrote the marker and then removed it on the very next line -- the original RemoveAt was left in place under it -- so the feature compiled, self-reported success, and changed nothing a reader could see. Replace-and-keep versus write-then-remove is the whole difference between this feature existing and not.

DECISION: the drop-marker quote must be chosen for RETRIEVAL VALUE, not merely uniqueness, and centre-of-unit selection fails that test. WHEN: reviewing or refining CreateDropMarker, or reading a marker whose quote tells you nothing about what was dropped. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then judge a marker by ONE question -- could a reader paste this quote into --keep and get back the unit it stands for. Prefer a phrase from the unit's OPENING, where this catalogue puts its TAG and claim, and widen from there until unique; skip stopwords and punctuation-only fragments; and do NOT markerise the trailing meta-line that reports hidden DEV steps, since it is not content and stands for nothing retrievable. WHY: measured live 2026-09-04, first build with markers shipped. The implementation picked words around the CENTRE of the dropped unit and produced ellipsis then quote hidden dash dash in BOTH proto-to-live-wiring and haiku-reflection -- the same fragment in two different skills, lifted from the parenthetical DEV-steps-hidden notice -- and ellipsis then quote sequence by in a third. Each is genuinely unique within its read and each is worthless to paste. Uniqueness was the constraint the code satisfied; usefulness was the requirement nobody encoded. The mechanism is correct and live -- markers replace units, stay, and keep every read under the ceiling at 28761 to 29785 bytes -- so this is a refinement of selection, not a rebuild.

INCIDENT: the TeeTextWriter goalkeeper is NOT wired, and the record that called it wired was written from a green build rather than a run. WHEN: you are about to rely on the goalkeeper -- the claim that unwired commands are also protected by the net at the Console.SetOut boundary -- or you are about to describe any interception layer as installed. HOW: measure BYTES DELIVERED on an unwired command that greatly exceeds the ceiling. 'wkappbot suggest list --all' returned 209332 bytes with no elision and no footer, on the promoted binary AND on a fresh staging exe run by path, so the transport was not the explanation. Then grep the host for the assignment, not the declaration: Program.cs:20 declares 'internal static TeeTextWriter? ActiveTee = null' and NOTHING in csharp/src ever assigns it, which also means Program.Dispatch.cs:201-204 never sets ExitCode on any tee and never disposes one; the only TeeTextWriter instances are built inside EyeCmdPipeServer.Dispatch.cs and AppBotEyeGlobalMode.cs, so the ordinary direct-core path installs no tee at all. WHY: a net hung in one room is not a net, and the ExitCode contract that promises a FAILED run keeps every byte is reading a field that is never set -- so the one guarantee protecting a failing command's output is inert. The general rule, which cost a day here: a module is wired when the production host greps positive for a CALL to it, and a declaration, a green build, a passing self-test and a DEPLOYED line are each compatible with nothing being wired at all.

DECISION: this engine's defects have all been ONE shape -- a mandatory element that was not paid for before the budget was spent, or a limit that was worked around instead of announced. WHEN: you are about to add anything to this engine that must ALWAYS appear, or you are about to make a limit hold by adding a condition that skips the check. HOW: reserve the element BEFORE allocation and let the plain fit test stand, or if a floor genuinely cannot move, ANNOUNCE it on stderr the way ReadFormatter.FloorNotice.cs does; read wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto and prove the change by BYTES DELIVERED on a real large read, never by reading the diff. WHY: measured across one day, 2026-09-04, four instances of the same disease at four layers. (1) The reserve counted only the tail, so the head's unbounded Desc and Tags pushed output past the ceiling and it spilled. (2) The unmatched-keep-term report was made mandatory by ORing its presence into the fit check, which cancelled the check and turned a spill into a thrown assertion -- while the correct reservation already existed a hundred lines above. (3) The 1000-byte content floor in ReadFormatter.cs was correct and silent, so a caller asking for 500 received 2527 and could not know. (4) The drop marker was fixed to quote a unit's OPENING, and the opening turned out to be the engine's own '[Item N]' label, so every marker named a number instead of content. Each was invisible in review and obvious in one measurement. THE TEST THAT CATCHES ALL FOUR: run it at a budget far below the floor and at one far above, and read what the output actually SAYS about itself.

DECISION: the guarantee is NEVER EXCEED IN SILENCE, not never exceed -- and the goalkeeper is the last line that enforces it, so it must see WriteLine and must judge at the END. WHEN: you are changing the byte ceiling, the goalkeeper, or the smoke that guards them; or you are about to write a check that fails a read merely for being larger than its budget. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then measure an UNWIRED command -- 'bin/wktest-core-manual-vX.Y.Z.exe suggest list --all 2>/dev/null | wc -c' -- because every wired command passes by construction and proves nothing about the net. A run over budget PASSES if the stderr notice fired and FAILS if it was quiet. WHY: measured 2026-09-04. The goalkeeper caught nothing for three reasons at once: BufferForGoalkeeper was wired into ConsoleWrite but NOT ConsoleWriteLine, where nearly all output goes, so the ball passed beside the net; the gate ran at the FIRST flush, which arrives long before a command ends, read a nearly empty buffer and switched itself off for the rest of the run; and it could not have worked at all before today because the TeeTextWriter that installs it had not been constructed since a 2026-05-07 refactor deleted the assignment. Fixed, an unwired command went 58911 to 28993 bytes. Two further rules the same hour: a long-lived writer must never buffer, since the Eye daemon holds one for days and a Dispose-only net would swallow its whole output; and output ALREADY within budget must be written back byte for byte, because the split-and-rejoin pass normalises terminators and re-encodes, which pushed a 2813-byte read to 3302 and erased all 38 drop markers. The smoke sweep added the same day caught both regressions within minutes.

RESULT: the ceiling sweep now has a FOURTH caller and a falsifier that is SENSITIVITY rather than size, because a size assertion passed straight through the a11y read defect. WHEN: you are adding this engine to a new caller, or writing any check that claims a read fits its budget. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the refuses-not-reads discipline, then assert TWO things the old sweep did not -- that two budgets far apart return DIFFERENT sizes, and that the retrieval footer does not contain the goalkeeper's sentence about a log file; bin/wktest-smoke-elision.sh does both against a live WindowsTerminal grap and SKIPs when no terminal exists, since a check that accuses a correct binary because the desktop was empty is worse than none. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 on two staging binaries against the same window. The broken build returned 21866 bytes at --budget 500 and 21508 at --budget 30000 -- the SMALLER budget producing the LARGER output -- while the fixed build returned 1266 and 3592, so the new check REFUSES the broken build and accepts the fixed one, which is the only verification that counts. The old sweep could never have caught it: every run sat under 30000 because the TeeTextWriter net was bounding the output, so the ceiling always looked healthy while the caller budget was reaching nothing. A version bump had been gated on this caller's sweep reporting zero over-ceiling, and that caller was not in the sweep at all -- a zero from a check that never ran the case is not evidence of absence. THE GENERAL RULE: when two LAYERS can produce the same visible outcome, assert on what only the correct layer can do -- here, respond to the budget and name a retrieval command that runs -- never on the outcome they share.

INCIDENT: I reported a live [Item N] label leak that does not exist in current source -- it is the DEPLOYED core, and the staging binary is already clean. WHEN: you see any formatter defect in ordinary session output and are about to file it or fix it. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wkappbot-build-verify-workflow, then reproduce the SAME command through the staging binary by path before writing a single word about it -- bare wkappbot goes through the launcher into a running core holding the PREVIOUS image, so what you are looking at may be a build you already fixed. WHY: measured 2026-09-05, both within one minute. wkappbot skill read wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate --budget 3000 returned entries prefixed with the engine label, verbatim '[Item 13] 13. CROSS-VERIFICATION 2026-07-14', while the identical command on bin/wktest-core-manual-v7.9.180.exe returned a grep count of ZERO for that pattern. Grepping the engine confirms it: the only occurrences of the label in csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI are two COMMENTS explaining why it must not be emitted, and nothing constructs it. So the leak is real for every session using the wrapper today and is ALREADY FIXED in staging -- which turns it from a bug to file into an argument for promoting. THE GENERAL RULE, and it is the same one that cost a predecessor a day: a defect observed through the wrapper is a statement about the DEPLOYED image, never about your source. I filed half a suggest on it before checking, which is the cost of skipping the two-binary comparison that takes one command.

RESULT: --keep steers WHICH unit survives and, since 2026-09-06, WHERE INSIDE that unit the reader is pointed -- before this, a kept-by-match unit was still rendered from its head, so a term deep in a long unit was chosen and then cut away. WHEN: a caller passes --keep and the matched word does not appear in the output, or a smoke run reports the term appearing zero times both with and without the flag. HOW: the selection pass records which term matched each kept unit and the render pass places a window CONTAINING that match, marked at the front so a mid-unit window is not mistaken for a unit head; units kept for any other reason still render from the head, and a unit whose match cannot be located falls back to head truncation. WHY: measured on wktest-core-manual-v7.9.196. The word floor occurs eight times in opus-self-reflection and a budget-6000 read with --keep floor returned it ZERO times, truncating at 'which is most of why this core reads at' while the original continues 'roughly 266KB and scores 69 against a 70 floor' -- one word short. After the fix the same read reports the term 7 times against 0 without it, which is the assertion in bin/wktest-smoke-elision.sh, and that check had been blocking every promotion. KNOWN WEAKNESS, silent rather than loud: the match is located by splitting on whitespace and re-deriving offsets assuming ONE separator per gap, so a run of whitespace drifts the index and the reader silently gets head truncation again; build the window from the match offset directly instead. The window function lives in ReadFormatter.MatchWindow.cs, extracted because the host refuses growth past 400 lines.

TODO: rebuild the --keep match window from the MATCH OFFSET, never by re-splitting on whitespace. WHEN: fixing ReadFormatter.MatchWindow.cs TruncateWithMatchWindow, or reviewing any window that reports a position it did not receive. HOW: run wkappbot skill read read-formatter-auto-elision for the elision contract, then derive both window bounds arithmetically from the index the search already returned, keep the public signature and return shape unchanged, and keep the replacement no longer than what it replaces because fat-source-growth refuses any growth of an oversized host. THE CONTRACT: given a match at index i in the unit text, the window is a pure function of i and the budget -- it must never re-derive i from the text, so multiple consecutive spaces, tabs and a leading indent all produce the SAME window as a single space would.
